newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Chamber of Commerce calls for price stability.
newsitem.headline: Thai Chamber of Commerce calls for price stability.

text.p: The Thai Chamber of Commerce on Monday asked members to help keep prices stable to counter the risk of rising inflation after the baht's defacto devaluation.
"We believe that the measure (to float the baht) will lead to higher production costs and could lead to higher inflation," said Vichien Tejapaiboon, president of the TCC.
"Therefore, I would like to ask for your cooperation to help minimise the effect on consumers," he said in a letter to members obtained by Reuters.
He urged members to keep prices of products in stock unchanged and "reasonably" increase prices of products imported after the baht's managed float last Wednesday.
The Bank of Thailand scrapped its 13-year-old tightly controlled exchange rate regime and allowed the baht to fall by between 15 and 20 percent in a managed float system.
Analysts and economists fear the move will send import bills soaring, especially for oil, and fan inflation which could override the benefits from the float.
